newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen higher if inflation data tame.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen higher if inflation data tame.

text.p: Wall Street stocks will take direction from consumer prices and retail sales data to be released by the government before the market open on Friday.

If the data point to tame inflation, stocks and bonds could rally and the Dow Jones Industrial Average could mark new highs. Yesterday, the Dow settled at 5772, up 17, just shy of May 22's record closing high of 5778.
The August Consumer Price Index (CPI), due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, and the "core rate," excluding food and energy, are both expected to rise 0.2 percent.
Retail sales for August will be released at the same time. Economists expect a climb of 0.7 percent. The core rate, excluding autos, is expected to add 0.4 percent.

"A lot will depend on the numbers. A good CPI and benign retail sales would mean another rally in the bond market, and would trigger a rally in stocks," said Hildegard Zagorski, a Prudential Securities market analyst.
"I'm fairly optimistic. I don't think we will see anything terrible in the CPI or sales, so we could get a rally and we may even see the Dow make a new high," she said.

Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said investors would more keenly eye the retail sales data, after Thursday's PPI hinted the CPI would probably fall in line with expectations.

"If they come out on target as expected, I suspect we'll make another attempt and trade in new high territory. If the numbers are too strong, we'll see a weaker opening and a sloppy day for stocks," Cardillo said.

"Yesterday's fizzle from the record high was somewhat surprising," he said. "Most of that was computer-related selling, and I suspect it may have been somewhat related to next week's triple witching expiration of options," he said.
The long bond was off 4/32 to yield 7.09 percent and S&P December futures were off 0.9 to 677.2.
Tokyo stocks soared to close nearly two percent higher on Friday with the 225-share Nikkei average up 398.71 points to 20,843.
In London, the FTSE edged up two to 3.934. U.S. stocks in London were slighly higher, extending yesterday's rally.
The dollar moved off lows it hit earlier after the release of Japan's second quarter growth data came within expectations.

Some investors are betting Bay Networks could emerge from its slump, but others say it may be to early to start betting on a comeback, according to the Wall Street Journal's "Heard on the Street" column.
